This is NOT presented as a clean uncomplicated sweep: the human volumetry cohort-dependent tension (§6), the toy model's own finite-capacity/timing trade-off (§9), the un-verified rat-specific liver:bodyweight percentage, and the genuinely-open termination-mechanism question are all disclosed, not smoothed over.

symmetric_qc_open_items: The F3 forced-adversary test (§5.5 of the doc) rules out specifically a 'deficit-BLIND, fixed magnitude regardless of resection extent' mechanism -- it does NOT separately build and force a DIFFERENT alternative: a 'one-shot' injury signal whose INITIAL amplitude scales with resection severity, with no ongoing/continuous mass-sensing afterward. Partial, indirect (reasoned, not separately measured) evidence against it: the robustness sweep shows the deficit-gated model converges to m* under independent +/-30% perturbation of the UPSTREAM trigger rate constants, a property a pure well-tuned one-shot dose would not obviously share -- flagged as a genuine, open limitation of the F3 argument's scope, not overclaimed as exhaustive.

The 3-state cascade is an illustrative TOY model -- its rate constants are disclosed-tuned to hit the live-verified TIMING anchors (~24h rat, ~36-48h mouse), NOT independently measured TNF/IL-6 blood-concentration kinetics (which peak an order of magnitude faster per this repo's own acute_phase_inflammation.py human-endotoxemia anchors).

This single-transient-pulse cascade has a FINITE total growth capacity and, once calibrated to the ~24h timing anchor, permanently settles ~4-5% short of m*=1 even at very long simulated time -- a genuine, diagnosed model limitation (not hidden): pushing capacity higher closes this gap but pulls the predicted peak below the live-verified band, a disclosed trade-off resolved here by prioritizing the externally-anchored timing falsifier.

The termination signal's MOLECULAR identity is explicitly NOT resolved -- this doc's geometric argument shows SOME deficit-sensing mechanism is structurally required (the fixed-program adversary necessarily mis-hits away from its calibration point), not which molecule implements it (endocan, hyaluronic acid, Hippo/YAP, metabolic-demand-sensing are all named as open literature candidates, none adjudicated here).

The human CT/MRI volumetry evidence shows a genuine, UNRESOLVED cohort-dependent tension: Gruttadauria 2012 (n=70) shows 37.1% of patients at or above 100% regeneration by ~2 months, while Nadalin 2004 (n=27) plateaus at 83% of original volume even at 1 year -- plausible reconciling factors (resection extent, MRI vs CT, cohort heterogeneity) are named but NOT adjudicated.

A rat-specific liver-to-bodyweight-ratio PERCENTAGE was not independently live-verified this session (targeted PubMed searches did not land a clean primary reference table) -- the qualitative '100%, precisely' hepatostat claim is well multiply-verified; the specific rodent percentage figure is honestly not forced.

Higgins & Anderson 1931, Grisham 1962, and Bucher & Swaffield 1964 are all bibliographically verified only (no live-extractable abstract text, pre-abstracting-era papers) -- a disclosed gap matching this repo's own established pattern.

Genetic knockout evidence (Cressman 1996 IL-6-KO; Yamada 1997 TNFR-I-KO) shows SEVERELY IMPAIRED, not abolished, regeneration -- correctly reported as such, not oversold into 'IL-6/TNF are the single non-redundant switch' (Fausto 2006's own explicit redundancy caveat is quoted verbatim).

Rodent-only mechanism scope; human disease-state (cirrhosis/fibrosis/steatosis) regenerative reserve is explicitly out of scope (that is the pre-existing REGEN-LIVER-REGENERATION graph node's own clinical-outcome-prediction domain, not duplicated here).

This is compensatory hyperplasia (mass restored via enlargement of REMAINING lobes), explicitly NOT epimorphic/blastema regeneration (which rebuilds the missing structure's own shape in place) -- precise on this distinction, deliberately avoiding salamander-limb overreach, per the task's own explicit framing.
